headline: Ansar Allah attempting large-scale attack. Single-chain (coalition spokesperson via Al Jazeera).
dek: Coalition spokesperson: forces engaged in heavy fighting with Ansar Allah in Kahboub (southwest Yemen), attempting to repel a 'large-scale attack'; situation described as 'very dangerous' with 'intense Ansar Allah bombardment'; clashes ongoing under 'intensive air cover' by coalition and Yemeni government…
sources: Saudi-led coalition spokesperson (statement via Al Jazeera, Oct 21)
fault_line: Is the coalition holding the line in the south — or is the Ansar Allah second front about to crack it?

sections.what_happened: Coalition spokesperson: forces engaged in heavy fighting with Ansar Allah in Kahboub (southwest Yemen), attempting to repel a 'large-scale attack'; situation described as 'very dangerous' with 'intense Ansar Allah bombardment'; clashes ongoing under 'intensive air cover' by coalition and Yemeni government forces. Same-day context (covered): Ansar Allah ballistic missile on Badr-camp Saudi ops room in Aden (1800-02); coalition says 4 drones intercepted over Medina/Eastern regions (Saree denies).
sections.what_verified: None independent — single chain (coalition spokesperson); consistent with the day's documented escalation pattern (Aden strike, Shabwa toll 73).
sections.what_disputed: No Ansar Allah statement on Kahboub found; no independent casualty/territorial confirmation.
sections.why_matters: While the world watches Aden, the coalition says its forces are in 'very dangerous' heavy fighting at Kahboub in the southwest under intensive air cover — the Yemen war is spreading beyond the cities into a second front.
sections.context: Background: Yemen — coalition claims heavy fighting with Ansar Allah in Kahboub (southwest): 'very dangerous' situation under 'intensive air cover'; Ansar Allah attempting large-scale attack. Single-chain (coalition spokesperson via Al Jazeera).

totw_analysis: Our read: While the world watches Aden, the coalition says its forces are in 'very dangerous' heavy fighting at Kahboub in the southwest under intensive air cover — the Yemen war is spreading beyond the cities into a second front. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is the coalition holding the line in the south — or is the Ansar Allah second front about to crack it?
